Differentiate $f(x) = (4x + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$f'(x) = \frac{3}{2}(4x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}} \times (4) = 6(4x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}}$$

Differentiate a second time to find $f''(x)$:
$$f''(x) = 6\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)(4x + 1)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \times (4) = 12(4x + 1)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{12}{\sqrt{4x + 1}}$$

Set up the common ratio condition for a geometric progression:
$$\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{T_3}{T_2} \implies \frac{18}{27} = \frac{4k}{18}$$
$$\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4k}{18} \implies 4k = 18 \times \frac{2}{3} = 12 \implies k = 3$$
